Hi Laura / Marissa,

We're kicking off the prep for the private deployment of Redwood in our production VPC. Per our onboarding call last week, the network/security team needs a consolidated checklist from Redwood so we can complete the firewall/IP allowlist, peering, and key management steps.

Can you send the canonical prerequisites (network and account items) and call out any items that require action from our side (e.g., public IPs, BGP config, certificate fingerprints)? Also please confirm whether Redwood requires a site-to-site VPN, direct connect, or just VPC peering for the initial go-live.

We'd like to get the allowlist updated and a validation window scheduled the week of Nov 22. Attaching our internal ticket for tracking: https://acmehealth.service-now.com/ticket/INC1234567

Thanks,
Dana Li

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is our onboarding prerequisites pack (RI-Private-Onboard-Prereqs.pdf) which covers:

- Account creation and IAM service account requirements
- IP allowlist ranges and outbound port requirements
- VPC peering vs. VPN/Direct Connect guidance and recommended SLOs
- KMS/HSM integration notes and JWT signing/certs requirements
- Audit log and retention expectations

Quick answers up front:
- We support VPC peering for initial go-live; for higher throughput or private interconnect you can provision Direct Connect (or equivalent) and we’ll switch routing.
- Allowlist: we need 3 static public egress IPs for callback/health checks and the peering CIDR for routing table entries. The exact ranges are in the attached PDF (section 2).
- KMS: you can bring your own key via AWS KMS or a customer-managed HSM. We’ll need the key arn and one-time CMK policy update during handoff.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Upload your network diagram and mark the preferred peering method.
2) Confirm a 2-hour validation window (we can do Nov 23 or 24 PT).
3) Provide the service account email we should add to org IAM (details in the attachment).

Looping Kar thik to coordinate the validation steps on our side; Marissa will drive the ops checklist.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0132

- We prefer VPC peering for the initial rollout; we have an existing Direct Connect circuit but want to keep that for higher-throughput stages.
- We'll provide the peering CIDR (10.84.0.0/16) and the list of NAT gateway public egress IPs once the ticket gets a thumbs-up.
- DMZ proxy sits in front of the compute tier; if Redwood needs to reach back into internal APIs, we can add a dedicated route through the proxy — please call this out in the validation checklist.

Thanks Dana/Michael — this is great. I pulled the diagram and the prerequisites together and sketched a minimal validation playbook below so your network team knows what we will run during the 2-hour window. Please confirm any local firewall rules or proxy behaviors that would impact these checks.

Validation playbook (high level):
- Pre-check (30m): confirm peering status, route tables, and IP allowlist present. Verify service account IAM and KMS access.
- Connectivity checks (30m): TLS handshake, mutual auth test to Redwood callback endpoint, health-check POST/GET to /status.
- Latency/throughput smoke (30m): run a short 100-request generation test at target sequence length to validate latency and look for egress bottlenecks.
- Log/audit verification (30m): confirm logs are being delivered to your syslog/s3 path and that audit entries include request ids.

Deliverables from Redwood during window:
- Temporary test service account and a short-run script (we will provide).
- IPs and FQDNs we will use for callbacks: (in attachment mop-network-clearance.txt)
- A short runbook for rollback if proxies break flow (we'll provide one).

Open items for ACME:
- Finalize whether callbacks go through the DMZ proxy (if yes, we need the proxy TLS interception cert or a bypass route).
- Confirm the three egress IPs to add to the allowlist.
- Provide the KMS CMK arn and confirm a one-time policy change window during handoff.

Once Dana confirms the above we will:
1) Post a short mutual action plan to the shared Drive (link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRI-MAP)
2) Schedule the two-hour validation for Nov 24 09:00-11:00 PT

Thanks — looping Marissa for the MOP and to own the runbook during the test.

—Karthik
